title: The Floss Rule
rule: In a one-syllable word with one short vowel, double the last letter when it is f, l, s or z: ff, ll, ss, zz. Floss helps you remember. A few words are exceptions, like if, of, bus, yes and us.
trickText: Look at the end of the word. One short vowel, then the f, l, s or z sound? Double the last letter. Put a breve on the vowel.
say: Today's case: the floss rule. When a short word has one short vowel and ends with the f, l, s or z sound, we double the last letter. Like floss: f l o s s.

activities.instruction: Put a breve on the short vowel.
Listen to the word. Choose the ending: ff, ll, ss or zz.
